content:
Chandra: Quick follow-up to RFC #321 — we need a tiny control-plane contract that works the same for hosted/dedicated/private. Link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/321
Chandra: My proposal: expose two lightweight endpoints on the control plane shim: `/capabilities` and `/policy-hints`. They return what features the control plane supports and recommended fallbacks for clients.
Chandra: Example response we could standardize on:
```json
{
  "schema_version": "2026-03-01",
  "model_variants": ["redwood/gpt-4o", "redwood/gpt-4o-q4"],
  "kv_cache": "enabled",
  "batching": {"max_tokens": 2048},
  "fallbacks": {"cpu_fallback": false, "quantized_variant": "redwood/gpt-4o-q4"}
}
```
Alex: I like the simplicity. Two concerns: 1) auth differences for private (customer-managed KMS/STS) and 2) how we version the schema.
Maria: For private, the shim can return a signed capability blob instead of raw flags. That way Hosted can be plaintext, Private returns an attestation. TTL on that blob is important.
Sam: Add `X-Capabilities-Version` header and a short negotiation handshake. Clients should gracefully ignore unknown fields.
Alex: Also we should avoid clients making too many calls at runtime — cache responses and refresh on 401/403 or TTL expiry.
Jen: Observability note: instrument a `capabilities_source` tag (hosted|dedicated|private) and track fallback rates vs latency. Helps quantify cost/latency tradeoffs.
Arjun: Edge case: Private control plane might not have direct access to our model catalog (air-gapped). If we return pointers only, the runtime may misinterpret. Prefer returning explicit capability assertions (signed) + an optional local catalog checksum.
Chandra: Good point — proposal updated: capabilities = minimal boolean flags + optional `assertion` object when needed. Assertion format = signed JSON + `expires_at`.
Chandra: Example with assertion:
```json
{
  "schema_version": "2026-03-01",
  "kv_cache": "enabled",
  "assertion": {
    "signed_by": "customer-kms://projects/xyz",
    "payload": "eyJ...base64...",
    "expires_at": "2026-03-22T12:00:00Z"
  }
}
```
Alex: That covers compliance needs. We should add a small SDK helper: `cap = fetchCapabilities(); if (cap.assertion) verifyAssertion(cap.assertion);` and fall back if verification fails.
Maria: TTL semantics: default 5m for hosted, 1h for dedicated, customer-configurable for private (but max 24h). Document in the RFC.
Sam: Also add a `policy_hints` payload for recommended batching/quantization profile per model to allow clients to auto-tune without hitting control plane each request.
Ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary of control-plane /capabilities on staging at 2026-03-21T09:00Z. :rocket:
Jen: I'll add dashboards and a small alert if fallback rate > 0.5% in the first 24h.
Arjun: One more: include a `compatibility_matrix` entry for older runtimes so we can deprecate fields safely.
Chandra: OK, I'll add these items to RFC 321 as follow-up bullets (assertions, headers, TTLs, telemetry, SDK snippet, deprecation plan). Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
